Brian Keene [1586]: Hi, guys. Just to follow up on Paycor, is it still a low double-digit grower, or should we be modeling more in this 8% to 9% growth territory for this fiscal year?
Bob Schrader [1599]: Yeah, I think we generally said, Brian, we expect it to be double digits. I would tell you the revenue per client comments, you know, that we made related to maybe being a bit softer than our expectations. It was interesting. It was really across the board. Every line of business, we saw that. And same thing with PayCore. I do think we saw some similar trends with, you know, maybe not as much attachment up front than what we assumed. as well as maybe a little bit lower average deal size. So, hey, we'll see where it plays out as we get to the balance of the year, but I would still expect it to be, if not low double digits, high single digit grower as we move forward.
evidence.role: conditional worded Paycor outlook; earlier 8–9 actual not a confirmed forecast range

evidence.text:
Scott Wurzel [3279]: Hey, good morning, guys, and thanks for taking my questions here. Bob, just had a question on the sort of 3Q guide and calling for total revenue growth of 18%. I kind of do some back-of-the-envelope math and assume some degree of acceleration on the PEO side of the business as you lap the So MPP headwinds, you know, it implies not really too much change on the MS side. And I'm just trying to kind of square that with some of the timing around, you know, pay core form filing revenue that they show up in fiscal 3Q. So any, you know, color you can give on the different moving parts there would be super helpful.
Bob Schrader [3313]: Yeah, I mean, again, I don't want to get into the habit of giving quarterly guidance. We try to give you color, and obviously I try to set myself up so I can at least be in line with the numbers. So we expect the business, as you mentioned, you're going to see acceleration like we did this quarter with the PO in insurance. We're going to anniversary the annual enrollment in January and some of the headwinds from last year. And we're going to continue to make progress on pay core, the integration, the synergy realization where we've had success. You know, that revenue is going to start flowing into the back half of the year. So, you know, I'm sitting here in the middle of the year. We still have selling season. There's probably an element of conservatism in there, but we would expect the business to continue to accelerate.
evidence.role: revenue/PEO growth acceleration and contribution from synergies

unresolved_fields_or_policy: Separate the specific PEO forecast from general company growth; anniversary explanation not automatically condition.

evidence.text:
Jason Kupferberg [3435]: Good morning, guys. Thanks. So I'm wondering, just in the management solution segment, if you expect the organic growth rate to improve off the current 4% levels, just as we move into the second half. And then just, you know, any thoughts on a realistic organic growth rate for the MS business once you lap Paycor?
Bob Schrader [3458]: Yeah, I mean, we definitely expect it to get better in the back half of the year, Jason. I mean, I don't want to give a longer-term growth until we get through this year with the integration. And obviously, synergy realization plays into that. But we expect some modest acceleration to the organic growth rate in management solutions, probably moving closer towards the, you know, 5% range over time, but that definitely, there is some acceleration there in the back half of the year.
evidence.role: company confirmed organic MS growth; limited commitment toward five, not an exact point

unresolved_fields_or_policy: Do not convert movement toward 5 into an exact 5% promise or a two-ended range; resolve allowed shape plus qualifiers.
Current analyst 4% is not the new forecast.

evidence.text:
Jason Kupferberg [3491]: Understood, understood. And then I want to just ask a follow-up on PEO. I know we've talked about it already a lot on the call, but you're at 4.5% year-to-date, and you'll need to do, I guess, 7.5% in the second half to get to the lower end of the six to eight range that you're pointing us to. And obviously we know the lapping of the comps, et cetera. But, you know, maybe if you can just talk through any other factors driving the acceleration and just some commentary on your visibility to kind of get three points of acceleration from first half to second half.
Bob Schrader [3530]: Thank you. It's a good question. I would start with pointing to the three points of acceleration that happened this quarter relative to last quarter. Again, some of that is I know there's been some confusion around it and concern. A lot of it, there's strong execution there for sure. As I mentioned, we had double-digit demand and really strong retention again this quarter. Um, but, but some of it is just the easier compare Jason, as you move into the back half of the year. So we just anniversary in October, the annual enrollment. Last year, there were some headwinds from that. You know, that's probably only 25% of the MPP enrollment is in October. The rest of it is in January. So you're going to have another lapping or anniversary of the enrollment and the headwind from last year. So the comps are just going to get better. So it's a combination of the comps getting better and we continue to see strong execution in the business. As I mentioned, I mean, that 6% number was was weighted down from some of the challenges that we see in the agency. The PO grew high single digits in the quarter. So we feel really good about where we are with the PO and as we move into the back half of the year.
evidence.role: analyst proposed 7.5% H2 calculation and annual six-to-eight range; management discusses drivers without expressly confirming the calculated 7.5

unresolved_fields_or_policy: Do not treat a polite response or explanation of drivers as confirmation of the analyst calculation.
Whether the annual six-to-eight range is sufficiently confirmed must be adjudicated separately from 7.5; no numeric import into P2-03 without evidence.
